knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Grid squares have side length one unit.

![](images/12/12de309260b1715d15ce13eec952669c420e8c5b28b72c81ee91e6fdc8586aa4.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\mathbf{a}+\lambda\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\mathbf{a}$ from $O$, ending at $A$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OA} &=1\,(0, -4)=(0, -4). \\
\overrightarrow{AC} &=(-2, -4).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/b6/b645dbbf051645531468868abe2ee98661dccac2d8ed919284838e1735130e3e.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{b}$, whose grid displacement is $(-2, -4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{-2}{-2}=1 \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-4}{-4}=1
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{b}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{AC}=\mathbf{b}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AC} \\
&=\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \\
&=\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=1$.

conversions: Reduce grid displacement ratio to a positive rational scalar

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Grid squares have side length one unit.

![](images/1f/1f9261a9f8942974cec8007bf68df6016a969fc4b8bc4d1d06829d83978985f9.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{4}{3}\,(0, 6)=(0, 8). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(5, 5).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/cc/cc9fc009dd80125e5b885e2476f4bb0e97a09cdb0e86945256cf1ae3470165bd.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(2, 2)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}+\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a} \\
&=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=\frac{5}{2}$.
